nodes.label: Proposal: Harden Server Security
nodes.rationale: The server exposes known security flaws: hardcoded secrets in config/config.js, wildcard CORS, password transported inside the AES token, wrong HTTP statuses (500 instead of 401/403) that can crash the process, and 50mb payload limits that ease DoS. These put credentials and the service at immediate risk.

nodes.label: Capability: secure-configuration
nodes.rationale: Loading of secrets and sensitive parameters via environment variables, with startup validation and no secrets in versioned source code.

nodes.label: Capability: request-security
nodes.rationale: Restrictive configurable CORS policy, safe payload limits, and authentication responses with correct HTTP status codes without leaking internal details.

nodes.label: D1: Native env reading without mandatory dotenv
nodes.rationale: config/config.js reads process.env directly with a requireEnv(name) helper that throws at startup if the variable is missing. dotenv as a mandatory dependency was rejected because it would be a new dependency in a legacy Node >= 6 project; .env.example documents the variables. Only direct-security variables (KEY_REQUEST_AUTH) are required; the rest have non-sensitive defaults or disable the feature (e-mail without credentials becomes sendEmail: false with a warning).
nodes.norm_label: d1: native env reading without mandatory dotenv

nodes.label: D2: CORS allowlist in existing manual middleware
nodes.rationale: Keep the manual middleware in index.js (no cors package) but echo the request Origin only when present in CORS_ORIGINS (comma split, trimmed); no match means no CORS headers. The cors package was rejected to minimize new dependencies since the manual middleware is about 10 lines.
nodes.norm_label: d2: cors allowlist in existing manual middleware

nodes.label: D3: Fix interceptor without changing token contract
nodes.rationale: Wrap CryptoJS.AES.decrypt + JSON.parse in try/catch returning 401 on failure; make the checkLogin callback fire on the failure path too (today only success invokes it, hanging the request); standardize 401 for missing/invalid token or rejected credentials and 403 for onlyLocalhost violations (was 500), with generic body via ResponseData.errorResponse. The AES token format (email+password inside) stays unchanged for client compatibility — redesigning it is a known weakness deferred to a future change.
nodes.norm_label: d3: fix interceptor without changing token contract

nodes.label: D4: Configurable payload limit with 1mb default
nodes.rationale: BODY_LIMIT with default '1mb' applied to bodyParser.json and bodyParser.urlencoded, replacing the 50mb limit that eased DoS. Deploys that genuinely need large payloads set the variable explicitly.
nodes.norm_label: d4: configurable payload limit with 1mb default

nodes.label: D5: Remove spawn monkey-patch and hardcoded gateway IP
nodes.rationale: The child_process.spawn monkey-patch (IIFE at the end of index.js) was debug instrumentation logging possibly sensitive arguments — removed entirely. The hardcoded internal IP 10.200.1.190 moves to GATEWAY_HOST/GATEWAY_PORT, with current values documented only in .env.example, not in code.
nodes.norm_label: d5: remove spawn monkey-patch and hardcoded gateway ip

nodes.label: KEY_REQUEST_AUTH Environment Variable
nodes.rationale: Encryption key for the request authentication token; the only mandatory environment variable — the server refuses to start without it, replacing the hardcoded keyRequestAutentication secret.

nodes.label: child_process.spawn Monkey-Patch (removed)
nodes.rationale: Debug instrumentation in index.js that logged all spawn arguments to the console, a potential leak of sensitive data; removed by this change.
